newsitem.title: JAPAN: Godo Steel says may tie up with Nakayama Steel.
newsitem.headline: Godo Steel says may tie up with Nakayama Steel.

text.p: Godo Steel Ltd is considering tying up with Nakayama Steel Products Co Ltd in the production and distribution of steel rods for construction use, a spokesman for Godo said on Wednesday.
Osaka-based Nakayama Steel Products is an unlisted maker of steel rods with annual sales of some 17 billion yen.
"We are negotiating a tie-up for steel rod production and distribution. We have not reached an agreement yet," the Godo Steel spokesman said.

Godo Steel, owned 9.9 percent by Nippon Steel Corp, posted a parent current loss of 4.88 billion yen in the year to March 1996, on sales of 86.24 billion yen, due to weaker market prices for steel rods. It has forecast a current profit of 1.4 billion yen for 1996/97.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun economic daily reported in its evening edition on Wednesday that Godo and Nakayama Steel would tie up in January next year and this step might eventually lead to a merger between the two companies.
"The story was speculation. We have not agreed yet and have no plans to merge," the spokesman said.
